newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Apasco seen raising Q4 sales.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Apasco seen raising Q4 sales.

text.p: Cement group Apasco will report higher fourth quarter sales and a strong profits rise, according to a Reuter survey of analysts.

A survey of six analysts gave an average earnings forecast of 3.73 pesos per share in 1996, against 0.396 of a peso the previous year. The 1995 figure was restated in end-1996 pesos for comparative purposes, as is common in Mexican accounting.

"Apasco's annual sales will rise 23 percent (over 1995), operating profit will go up 93 percent, with an operating margin of 28 percent in 1996 and net profit could grow more than eight times from 1995," said Gerardo Saenz at OBSA-GSerfin.
Saenz also estimated that the company would have a domestic sales volume of some 1.55 million tonnes in the fourth quarter of 1996, against 1.48 million in the same 1995 quarter.

"Because of the tendency (Apasco) has had in volumes it could do well in cement and premixed concrete," said Monica Lourdes De Leon, an analyst at BBV-Probursa. "That's one of the reasons why the market has paid a better price for Apasco's share than Cemex's".
However, the analysts said Apasco's fourth quarter margins would be hurt by a rise in natural gas prices -- one of the company's main costs.
This was likely to hurt Apasco more than Cemex because Apasco had cut prices more aggressively, they added.
After achieving prices of $79 per tonne in the third quarter, Apasco cut prices in the fourth quarter to recover lost market share.

Some analysts estimated that Apasco might have cut prices as low as $70 but in compensation could have won back one to two percentage points of market share. Cemex had snatched three percentage points of Apasco's market share in the third quarter.
"The price cut will reduce operating margins to around 25.5 percent in the fourth quarter," said OBSA-GSerfin's Saenz. Apasco reported margins of over 29 percent in the second and third quarters.
Claudia Gonzaalez of Abaco brokerage said Apasco's fourth quarter margin pressure had already been discounted in its current stock price.
"The market is not going to change the positive outlook it has for Apasco in 1997 because of a margin cut in the last quarter (of 1996)," she said.
